claim: Harry rates Palmer above Rogers as the better buy, in line with Fantasy Football Scout's projections, naming the Chelsea duo his top midfield picks given their lack of European football.
quote: I believe Palmer is better than Morgan Rodgers, and the Fantasy Football Scout contributor section also expects Palmer to be worth more than Rodgers

claim: Harry is unsure Saka is clearly better than Ødegaard or worth it over a triple Arsenal defence, but still rates him Arsenal's main goal threat ahead of Ødegaard and Tzolis.
quote: He is probably still their main threat from the game, despite Odegaard and Solanke looking good

claim: Harry ranks Havertz above the previous names but suggests cheaper alternatives (Gibbs-White, Ødegaard, Groß, Mbeumo, Gakpo or Rogers) to free funds for a triple Arsenal defence of Raya, Gabriel, Calafiori and Konsa.
quote: you could replace him with someone like Morgan Gibbs-White, Martin Odegaard, Pascal Gross, Brian Mbemo, Gakpo or Rodgers to free up funds to strengthen the defence

claim: Harry really likes Gibbs-White given four of Forest's next five (Villa, Coventry, Palace, Ipswich) look winnable, and rates his penalty duty and goal threat highly.
quote: Aston Villa, Coventry, Crystal Palace and Ipswich are four of the next five matches, and they are pretty good games where I think Gibbs-White can shine. It meets some standards. He takes penalties

claim: Harry notes Gibbs-White nearly assisted Forest's disallowed goal and thinks he'd get more credit if it had stood.
quote: He almost assisted that disallowed Nottingham Forest goal and if it had been counted I think a lot more people would have been talking about him

claim: Harry wants to see Arsenal's Champions League squad before fully trusting Ødegaard long-term, expecting slightly earlier substitutions, but still likes the risk at £6.6m.
quote: I want to see Arsenal's Champions League squad in midweek before I can decide whether he's a long-term starter... I think it's worth taking a bit of a risk

claim: Harry likes Groß in the number-ten role, noting he nearly scored again in round three.
quote: Since Gross left, I really like that he plays at the number ten position. He almost scored again in the 3rd round

claim: Harry presents Mbeumo as the cheaper alternative to Bruno Fernandes, backed by having the best xG/90 of any midfielder in the game.
quote: his expected goals (xG) per 90 minutes is the best among all midfielders in the game

claim: Harry flags that Gakpo reportedly didn't train with Liverpool ahead of their Champions League game as a precaution, with the reason unclear.
quote: it seems he didn't train with Liverpool before the Champions League game as a precaution. What does this really mean? We don't know

claim: Harry notes Liverpool have other winger cover if Gakpo needs a rest, but still rates him worth considering at 7.2m if available.
quote: when they have players like Rio, Bakuna, and on the right, like Minamino, there are plenty of wingers who can play if Gakpo needs a rest

claim: Harry isn't worried about Sangaré's early substitution, calling it a bad day rather than a lost role, and still rates his attacking potential and price highly.
quote: I know he was replaced early, but I wouldn't let that worry you. It was just a bad day for him. He's still great for his price

claim: Harry weighs Barnes against Elanga: Elanga is pricier and more stable, but Barnes offers more big-haul upside as shown in round three.
quote: Elanga is a little more expensive, maybe a little more stable, but Barnes has a little more potential for a big point when he wants to

claim: Harry names João Pedro his number-one overall pick this week at 7.7m, citing fixtures, form and no European football, while acknowledging his own Chelsea bias.
quote: this is Joao Pedro. Its price is 7.7 million. The upcoming matches, performance and lack of European competition make him such a great choice

claim: Harry's main doubt on Isak is whether he keeps full minutes at home to Fulham if Gakpo sits out the midweek Champions League game; he still expects Isak to start but flags an early-substitution risk like in GW3.
quote: if Hakpo doesn't play in the Champions League in midweek, and Isak is likely to have to play 90 minutes... as we saw in the 3rd round, he could be traded early

claim: Harry says Isak is clearly Liverpool's best striker option if affordable alongside Haaland and João Pedro; otherwise he suggests Wissa or Barry.
quote: If you can afford him, he is clearly Liverpool's best striker to choose. If not, I would look at Yoan Vissa or Brian

claim: Harry says Barry leads all strikers, and even ranks ahead of Haaland, Isak and João Pedro, in expected goals per 90 this season, but needs a lot of xG to convert given his poor finishing.
quote: he even leads in expected goals (xG) per 90 minutes this season among all strikers, and I think among all players he is even higher than Haaland, Isaac and Joao Pedro

claim: Harry likes Barry's next three (Spurs, Ipswich, Hull) before tougher games against Chelsea and Arsenal, suggesting a pricier alternative if affordable or Barry as the cheaper rotation option.
quote: In their next three games they play Spurs, Ipswich and Hull, which is good... if you have the money, I would go for Westergaard, but Barry is a good cheaper option

claim: Harry expects Havertz's minutes to be managed once the Champions League starts, predicting another Arsenal forward gets more starts since Havertz can't play twice a week all season.
quote: once the Champions League starts I think we'll see someone like Deukeresch appearing more often for Arsenal and getting more minutes

claim: Harry flags Gonzalo Garcia's tough next two (Liverpool, Man Utd) but says he becomes a genuine budget rival to Barry and Wissa from round six.
quote: from the sixth round onwards, Ipswich, Holland and Coventry will definitely be in the sights to compete with Barry and Yoan Wyssa for a lower price

claim: Harry likes Calvert-Lewin's next two home games (Newcastle, Palace) but flags he faces Chelsea on Wednesday night, worth monitoring for fatigue or rotation.
quote: Home games with Newcastle and Palace in the next two rounds look very attractive. Of course, he plays Chelsea on Wednesday night, so it's worth keeping an eye on

claim: Harry flags two further, pricier forward options but says their tough upcoming games (Chelsea/Villa/Liverpool and Man Utd/Chelsea) make them hard to recommend as buys right now.
quote: Two more to watch out for are Diogo and Mope. The problem is that they are too expensive... it's hard to recommend them as a buy

claim: Harry has already confirmed his own transfers for the week but says he's still tempted by a wildcard, having lost value on players he doesn't own such as Wissa.
quote: I have already confirmed my transfers, but part of me is still thinking about a wild card for round 4... I have lost quite a lot in recent days due to the change in the value of players like Wiss

claim: Harry's overall summary: focus heavily on Arsenal defenders (probably three), Chelsea in midfield, and Haaland/João Pedro plus Isak, Wissa or Barry up front depending on budget.
quote: in attack - Haaland, Joao Pedro, and then Isak, Wissam or Barry, depending on your budget. These are my top players to buy
